scenes.label: Day 2 · JS interview prep
scenes.title: Why does this function crash?
scenes.say: Day two of JavaScript interview prep. Why does this function crash?
We call greet before it's defined, using a const arrow function. Boom. Reference error.
Now the same thing with a regular function. It works, and prints hi.

scenes.label: why it happens
scenes.title: It's hoisting
scenes.say: Here's why. Function declarations are fully hoisted, body and all. const is hoisted too, but stays in the temporal dead zone until that line runs.

scenes.label: interview rule
scenes.text: Define const functions before calling them.
scenes.say: The rule: define const functions before you call them.
So does var get hoisted too? Drop your answer in the comments, and follow for day three.
